quote: panels, battery backup panels, and all that, and I'm interested.
stewart_read: Customer arrives already wanting the Powerwall battery specifically — a strong buying signal the rep should have leaned into rather than treating as a routine verify item.
coaching_implication: Rep confirmed the Powerwall availability but didn't build on the enthusiasm with a forward-pulling hook (e.g., tying battery backup to his bill pain).

quote: This is calling with Ion. I got a request to look at a disclaimer for your line.
stewart_read: The intro is garbled and never clearly states who Ion is or how the lead was sourced (Tesla referral, form-fill, etc.) — legitimacy is not established cleanly in the first 30 seconds.
coaching_implication: Even with a warm customer, a clean company/lead-source statement should be the first sentence, not buried in unclear phrasing.

stewart_read: Customer discloses a $400/month bill — a strong anchor — but the rep's response is generic and non-committal.
coaching_implication: The bill should have been flipped into alignment-against-the-utility per objection_inversion; instead it was acknowledged and dropped.

quote: Oh my goodness. 400. Okay. Yeah. We'll definitely help you get that cut down.
stewart_read: Rep reacts to the bill number but files it rather than using it to pull the customer toward the appointment ('that's exactly why the closer needs to show you the real numbers').
coaching_implication: A stronger move ties the $400 bill directly to booking urgency instead of a generic reassurance.

quote: I'm a retired disabled veteran and retired Connecticut state employee.
stewart_read: Customer discloses veteran/disabled/fixed-income status as context for why he doesn't track his credit — a vulnerability disclosure the rep does not acknowledge before pivoting straight to disqualifying him.
coaching_implication: This disclosure deserved acknowledgment before the credit conversation continued; instead the rep used it as further justification to tell him to wait.

quote: I would wait to look into solar until you know that your credit is above $6.70.
stewart_read: Rep unilaterally disqualifies on stated (not pulled) credit and advises the customer to walk away, per the schema's open policy question this may be killing a real deal rather than following confirmed procedure.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may be following a real hard-DQ policy to avoid wasting a closer's time on an unqualified lead. Reactive read: rep guessed/assumed poor credit from 'I have no idea' and closed the door without offering to book anyway and flag for the closer's pull.
coaching_implication: Absent confirmed policy that setters DQ on stated credit, the rep should have booked and flagged for the closer's actual credit pull instead of telling the customer to wait.
